steps.title: Prepare photolithography layers
steps.instruction: Spin‑coat each SU‑8 layer on a silicon wafer using the manufacturer’s spin protocol (10 s spread, then 30 s spin) at the speeds and times listed, then perform edge‑bead removal and bake as described.

substeps.instruction: Conduit layer: SU‑8 2002, 1 000 rpm → 2.4 µm height.
Spotting region layer: SU‑8 2005, 2 600 rpm → 4.8–5 µm height.
HD biopixel layer: SU‑8 2007, 1 000 rpm → 12 µm height.
Minor channel layer: SU‑8 2075, 4 000 rpm → 60–65 µm height.
Major channel layer: SU‑8 2075, 2 400 rpm on top of undeveloped major channel layer, include 1 h edge‑bead removal at 40 °C on a hot plate using Edge Bead Remover (EBR) PG → final height 145–170 µm.

steps.title: Mix and degas PDMS
steps.instruction: Combine Sylgard 184 elastomer base and curing agent, degas, and keep the mixture bubble‑free before casting.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 70 g Sylgard 184 base into a weigh boat and add 7 g curing agent.
Mix thoroughly with a clean glass stir rod for ~3–5 min.
Place the mixture in a vacuum desiccator; vent periodically to avoid overflow and remove all bubbles.

steps.title: Prepare aluminum foil casting dish
steps.instruction: Cut and fold aluminum foil to create a shallow bowl around a glass plate for PDMS casting.

substeps.instruction: Cut a 16 in × 16 in piece of foil and fold twice to obtain an 8 in × 8 in square.
Place the 5 in × 5 in glass plate in the centre, fold up the foil edges to form a bowl, overlapping the foil over the plate edges to prevent PDMS leakage.

steps.title: Cast PDMS onto wafer
steps.instruction: Pour bubble‑free PDMS onto the photopatterned wafer inside the foil dish, degas again, and bake.

substeps.instruction: Place the wafer in the centre of the foil dish and pour the PDMS mixture over it.
Degas the wafer‑PDMS assembly in a vacuum desiccator until all bubbles disappear (≈30 min–1 h); keep the chamber level.
If needed, recenter the wafer with two pipette tips and press gently on opposite sides to ensure even contact and remove any PDMS that seeped underneath.
Bake the wafer stack in a level oven at 95 °C for 1 h (PDMS shrinkage is accounted for at this temperature).

steps.title: Release PDMS device from wafer
steps.instruction: Peel the cured PDMS off the wafer, cut individual chips, and create inlet/outlet ports.

substeps.instruction: Peel off the aluminum foil and trim excess PDMS around the wafer with a razor blade (horizontal slide only; avoid angling to prevent wafer breakage).
Slide the razor blade between wafer and glass plate to separate them.
Remove any excess PDMS from the wafer backside with the razor blade.
Peel the PDMS from the feature side in the direction of the major channels.
Place the PDMS feature‑side up on a cutting mat and cut out each device with a razor blade.
Punch inlet and outlet holes using a 0.5 mm biopsy puncher.

steps.title: Clean PDMS devices
steps.instruction: Rinse, dry, and tape‑clean the PDMS chips to remove debris.

substeps.instruction: Rinse devices with 70 % ethanol and blow dry with compressed air or nitrogen.
Clean the feature side four times and the non‑feature side twice with Scotch tape, pressing gently with forceps to lift debris.
Leave a fresh piece of tape on each side for storage; devices may be stored up to two months.

steps.title: Clean glass slides
steps.instruction: Sonicate glass slides in Helmanex III solution, rinse, and dry.

substeps.instruction: Sonicate slides in 2 % Helmanex III for 30 min at 40 °C.
Rinse with deionized water while rubbing with a clean nitrile glove.
Dry completely with pressurized nitrogen; ensure no streaks.
Store clean slides in a dust‑free Petri dish until use.

steps.title: Prepare media recipes
steps.instruction: Make all required liquid and solid media according to the listed formulations.

substeps.instruction: Standard YPD (1 L): 10 g yeast extract, 20 g peptone, 20 g glucose; autoclave.
Standard SC agar (1 L): 6.7 g YNB, 2 g SC powder, 900 mL deionized water; adjust pH to 5.6 with 10 N NaOH, add 16 g agar, autoclave 121 °C 20 min, cool to ~50 °C and add 20 g glucose.
Microfluidic media (1 L): 6.7 g YNB without riboflavin/folic acid, 2 g SC powder, 20 g glucose, 0.5 mL Tween 20, 2 % Helmanex III solution, 98 mL deionized water, 2 mL Helmanex solution; mix.

steps.title: Prepare SC agar Plus plates
steps.instruction: Dispense SC agar into Singer Plus plates and dry before storage.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 42 mL SC agar into each Plus plate on a level surface.
Allow plates to dry on the benchtop with lids covered for 48 h.
Cover with Parafilm and store at 4 °C (up to 6 months).

steps.title: Grow yeast overnight in 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Inoculate each well with a yTRAP strain and incubate in YPD.

substeps.instruction: Add 200–300 µL of each strain to wells of a 96‑well plate.
Incubate overnight at 30 °C with shaking.

steps.title: Spot cultures onto SC agar Plus plates
steps.instruction: Use the Singer ROTOR to transfer liquid cultures onto agar and grow.

substeps.instruction: Load the 96‑well plate onto the ROTOR and spot onto the SC agar Plus plate using default pinning settings for source and target.
Incubate spotted plates at 30 °C for 2 days.

steps.title: Re‑array onto 1536‑density plates
steps.instruction: Transfer colonies from the 96‑agar plate to four 1536‑density SC agar plates with the Singer Stinger.

substeps.instruction: Pick colonies with the Stinger and spot onto four 1536‑density plates that match the microfluidic layout.
Grow overnight at room temperature.
Store 1536 plates in the fridge (up to 6 months).

steps.title: Replicate 1536 plates onto SC agar
steps.instruction: Create fresh SC agar copies of the four 1536 plates and heat‑shock the cells.

substeps.instruction: Using the ROTOR Replicate program, copy each 1536 plate onto a new 1536‑density SC agar plate.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight (heat‑shock required for viability).

steps.title: Combine 1536 plates into 6144 plate
steps.instruction: Array the four 1536 plates onto a single 6144‑density SC agar plate using the 1:4 program and specified pinning parameters.

substeps.instruction: Set pinning pressure 58 % (source) → 50 % (target), speed 64 mm/s (source) → 100 mm/s (target), overshoot 19 mm (source) → 10 mm (target), and contact time 0.6 s for both source and target.
Execute the 1:4 array program to produce the 6144‑density plate.

steps.title: Spot alignment markers on acrylic tool
steps.instruction: Transfer cells from the 6144 plate onto the acrylic alignment tool using the Replicate program.

substeps.instruction: Load the 6144 plate as source and the acrylic tool as target; use the pinning settings listed in Table 1.

steps.title: Align PDMS to acrylic alignment tool
steps.instruction: Place the PDMS device onto the acrylic tool under a mask aligner and secure with tape.

substeps.instruction: Set the acrylic tool on the mask holder with cells facing up.
Remove scotch tape from one PDMS device (avoid touching the feature side).
Place the PDMS feature‑side up over the alignment cells, centering the spotting regions.
Apply fresh scotch tape on top of the PDMS and press gently to ensure adhesion.
Repeat for each device.

steps.title: Oxygen plasma treatment
steps.instruction: Expose the glass slide and PDMS‑acrylic stack to plasma to activate surfaces.

substeps.instruction: Place the 1 in × 3 in glass slide and the PDMS‑acrylic stack in the plasma chamber.
Expose to 30 W oxygen plasma for 30 s.
Blow off any dust with compressed nitrogen.

steps.title: Spot cells onto plasma‑treated PDMS
steps.instruction: Transfer cells from the 6144 plate onto the plasma‑treated PDMS‑acrylic stack, then bond to glass.

substeps.instruction: Using the ROTOR with Table 1 parameters, spot cells onto the PDMS‑acrylic stack.
Peel the PDMS off the acrylic tool.
Place the PDMS face‑down on the plasma‑treated glass slide; tap gently to promote bonding.
Incubate the assembled device at 37 °C for ≥2 h.

steps.title: Load and prime microfluidic chip
steps.instruction: Prepare the bonded chip for experiments by degassing and wetting.

substeps.instruction: Place the chip in a vacuum desiccator for 20 min.
Add at least 20 µL of microfluidic media to both inlet and outlet ports to wet the device.
